messages:
Emma (Support): heads up — we have a scheduled maintenance for runtime GPU kernel patch on Tue 2026-05-12 02:00–04:00 UTC. impact: short evictions of some Dedicated nodes for ~5–20m during kernel swap, fallback to hosted tiers expected. preparing customer-facing comms (status page + email + SMS). can someone draft snippets for EU/APAC local times and SMS?

Josh (Eng Release): putting together statuspage snippet now. quick question — do we want to call this a brief outage or ‘intermittent capacity reductions’? phrasing matters for SRE escalation.

Emma (Support): prefer "brief intermittent capacity reductions" with explicit expected duration. avoid the word outage unless we actually see >30m degraded. include rollback and pinning guidance.

Lina (Oncall): schedule is ok for our canary regions. note: start time shifts to 02:30 UTC for APAC teams to avoid overlap with another deploy. please update the time in templates.

Raj (SRE): add this line to status page: "If your traffic requires guaranteed tail-latency, consider pinning to Dedicated pool A (v1.4.3) for the window; our routing will prefer Hosted fallbacks automatically." also include contact for emergency SLA requests.

Josh (Eng Release): draft status page snippet (plain):
```
Starting Tue 12 May 02:30 UTC (localized below) we will perform a kernel patch on a subset of GPU hosts. Customers may experience brief intermittent capacity reductions on Dedicated instances for ~5–20 minutes while nodes are drained and restarted. Hosted API and Dedicated fallbacks will remain available.

Regions & local times:
- UTC: 02:30–04:30
- CET: 04:30–06:30
- AEST: 12:30–14:30

What we're doing: applying a security/stability kernel patch to improve GPU driver reliability.

Mitigation: automatic routing to compatible model variants and hosted capacity. Customers can pin to Dedicated pool A (v1.4.3) to avoid routing changes during the window.

We will post updates here and on status.redwood.ai.
```

Emma (Support): looks good. now an email subject + short body for customers with Dedicated commitments. keep it concise.

Josh (Eng Release): email draft: 
Subject: Planned maintenance — brief Dedicated capacity changes on 12 May (UTC)
Body:
Hi {{customer_name}},

We’re applying a maintenance patch to our GPU hosts on Tue, 12 May from 02:30–04:30 UTC. During this window some Dedicated instances may be briefly drained and restarted (expected 5–20 minutes per host). Your service will failover to Hosted or other Dedicated pools where possible. No action is required unless you rely on pinned capacity.

If you require uninterrupted Dedicated throughput, reply to this email and we’ll coordinate a pin or exact SLA accommodation.

Thanks,
Redwood Inference Support

Emma (Support): add a short SMS template (160 chars). keep it urgent but calm.

Josh (Eng Release): SMS draft: "Redwood: Planned maintenance 12 May 02:30–04:30 UTC. Brief Dedicated capacity reductions possible. See status.redwood.ai for updates. Reply for pinning help."

Lina (Oncall): small nit — the SMS link should be shortened for SMS char limits: use rdw.ai/status. Also add an instruction for customers who have automated health-check integrations to expect transient 5xx from pinned endpoints.

Raj (SRE): suggest including rollback phrasing in the status page so customers know we may roll back the kernel if an issue occurs: "If we detect regressions, we will halt the rollout and roll back to the previous kernel; status updates will be posted to this page."

Emma (Support): good. also include a short JSON snippet for programmatic customers (webhooks) that we can paste into the email for ops teams. keep it compact.

Josh (Eng Release): programmatic webhook snippet: 
```json
{ "event": "maintenance", "start": "2026-05-12T02:30:00Z", "end": "2026-05-12T04:30:00Z", "impact": "intermittent_capacity_reduction", "recommendation": "pin_to_pool:v1.4.3 or use hosted_fallback" }
```

Emma (Support): perfect. ok next steps: - finalize localized times and translations (ES, FR, JA) — outreach to marketing. - schedule statuspage publish at 02:00 UTC with auto-updates during window. - prepare canned updates for the oncall to paste into status updates (OK/Degraded/Resolved).

Lina (Oncall): I’ll prep canned update strings:
- OK: "All systems normal."
- Degraded: "Customers in region X may see capacity reductions; mitigation in progress."
- Resolved: "Maintenance complete; normal routing restored."

DeployBot: Deploy scheduled: kernel-patch/v2 — start 2026-05-12T02:30:00Z. Canary plan: eu-west-1 -> eu-central-1 -> ap-southeast-2. Automated rollback on >3 canary failures.

SupportBot: Reminder queued: customer email batch will send 24h before start. SMS batch will send 2h before start.

Raj (SRE): final ask — include a short troubleshooting line for customers: "If you see prolonged errors >30m please open an urgent support ticket with trace id and region."

Emma (Support): will add that to all templates. thanks everyone — I’ll post the final drafts in #support-alerts channel 24h before send. :thumbsup:
